key_insight: A Bayesian finite-element inverse solver can reconstruct blood-flow velocity and pressure from sparse noisy measurements while also providing uncertainty estimates.
engineering_relevance: This enables clinically useful flow diagnostics on patient-specific vascular geometries without offline training data, improving reliability for quantities like pressure drop and wall shear stress.
method: Represent velocity and pressure with Taylor-Hood finite-element basis functions.
Impose physics-informed maximum-entropy priors and a noisy measurement likelihood to form the posterior.
Compute the MAP via a sparse nonlinear least-squares solve, eliminate pressure analytically, and use a Laplace approximation for uncertainty quantification.
evidence_signal: On patient-specific cerebral aneurysm, aortic aneurysm, and aortic coarctation cases, the method outperformed tricubic interpolation and matched a PINN for velocity/pressure reconstruction while estimating wall shear stress more accurately than both.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the assumed noise model and the quality of the finite-element discretization, and the approach is still tied to steady-flow assumptions.
paper_title: Bayesian finite element regression for vascular flow reconstruction with quantified uncertainty
